To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cross section for the quasielastic scattering in Ar-40 is reduced by about 20% compared to free nucleon case.

the nuclear effects in the cross sections are significant and that the ${\ensuremath{E}}_{\nu}$ dependence of the cross sections is different for the ${\ensure mathrm{q}e}$ and ${}^{\ensuremath{\mu}\nu}$ channels.

the quasielastic cross sections for the neutrino interactions in the nucleus are reduced due to the presence and motion of nucleons in a nucleus, and that the reduction is more pronounced for neutrino than for antineutrino interactions, and that the cross sections are sensitive to the nuclear structure of the target.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the neutrino cross section in a nucleus.
the study of neutrino-nucleon interactions at low energies.
the study of the neutrino absorption cross sections in the nuclei, and their dependence on the nuclear medium, in the context of atmospheric neutrino experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclear effects in Ar-40 do not change the cross section by more than a factor of two.
the cross sections in the nucleus are smaller than those in the free nucleon, and that the nuclear medium effects on the quasielastic cross sections are significant.

the cross sections for the neutrino-nucleus scattering in ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}$, ${}^{16}\mathrm{O}$, and ${}^{40}{\mathrm{Ar}}$ are not very different, and the differences between the cross sections in the three nuclei are not very significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear effects in ${}^{12}$C and ${}^{40}$Ar are very similar.
we have developed a method to compute the neutrino-nucleus cross section that takes all nuclear effects into account.

the nuclear effects are found to be significant for the ${\ensuremath{{}^{40}\text{Ar}}}$ nucleus, and the ${\ensureMath{\ensuremath{\nu_{\mu}}}}$ absorption cross-section is found to be larger than that of ${\ensureMath {\ensuremath{{\nu_{e}}}}}$ for neutrino energies below 1.5\,\ensuremath{\text{GeV}}.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nuclear effects are important and should be taken into account when extracting neutrino properties from atmospheric neutrino data.
the nuclear effects are not very large and can be absorbed into the effective axial mass $M_{A}^*$, which can be extracted from the data.
the nuclear effects reduce the inclusive cross section for ${}^{40}{\rm Ar}$ by a factor of 0.6 relative to the free-nucleon case.
